episode_summary: TBP88 (2016-09-22) interviews JJ (Christopher Jeffrey), engineer at Purse.io, about bcoin, his pure-JavaScript Bitcoin full node and library. Covers SPV vs full nodes, what a full node must do, JavaScript performance and security tradeoffs, the FindAndDelete and SIGHASH_SINGLE consensus quirks, BIP 151 encrypted peer-to-peer support, mining altcoins in the early days, and the Blight Lightning project built on bcoin.

cards.claim: JJ explained that Bitcoin has two kinds of nodes, light SPV nodes and full nodes.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: So there's two kinds of Bitcoin nodes. There's light nodes or SPV nodes, and then there's full nodes.

cards.claim: JJ described how an SPV wallet uses a Bloom filter of its addresses to ask peers for relevant transactions.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: So you put all of your addresses in your wallet into a Bloom filter and ask the network, you know, what transactions have these addresses in them, and peers send you those transactions.

cards.claim: JJ explained that a full node must implement all of Bitcoin Core's network-keeping behavior, not just the parts a wallet needs.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: So full nodes are a bit different. Full nodes are the full Bitcoin implementation.

cards.claim: JJ listed the duties of a full node as validating the blockchain, maintaining a mempool, and relaying transactions and blocks.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: So this includes validating the blockchain, maintaining a mempool, relaying transactions, relaying blocks, and things like that.

cards.claim: JJ argued that writing bcoin in JavaScript lets it run almost anywhere, including inside a browser.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: bcoin is written in javascript so the nice thing about bcoin um is that it's javascript

cards.claim: JJ explained that JavaScript objects live on a garbage-collected heap, so their memory is not zeroed the way crypto key material should be.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: in JavaScript, you're on a memory managed heap. So anything that you put onto the JavaScript heap, any JavaScript object, that is, you know, you can't control that.

cards.claim: JJ said bcoin calls native C++ crypto bindings when available and falls back to pure JavaScript when they are not.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: And it does that partly for security and partly for performance. If that binding is not available, it falls back to a pure JavaScript implementation.

cards.claim: JJ said JavaScript hash table keys must be strings, so binary data has to be converted to hex strings for lookups.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: hash table keys in JavaScript, they have to be JavaScript strings.

cards.claim: JJ claimed bcoin could process a modern one megabyte block in about 1.2 to 1.3 seconds.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: Bitcoin can process a modern one megabyte block in about 1.2, 1.3 seconds.

cards.claim: JJ described bcoin's wallet server as using BIP44 HD keys, with LevelDB in use and a planned switch to LMDB.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: It's HD keys with BIP44 derivation. It uses level DB right now, but I'm switching it to LMDB as a backend.

cards.claim: In September 2016 JJ said Jonas Schnelli came up with BIP 151, which adds peer-to-peer encryption to the Bitcoin protocol.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: jonas schnelly came up with the bit 151 a little while ago

cards.claim: JJ claimed bcoin was the first full or light node implementation with BIP 151 peer-to-peer encryption.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: Bitcoin is actually the first full or light node implementation that has peer-to-peer encryption.

cards.claim: JJ said he had previously worked on BitCore, the BitPay JavaScript library, before going independent with bcoin.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: BitCore which is the BitPay JavaScript library which is actually, I used to work on BitCore.

cards.claim: JJ stated that almost every alternative Bitcoin script implementation in small libraries violates consensus rules.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: I think almost every alternative Bitcoin script implementation I've seen in little libraries like this, pretty much all of them violate consensus rules.

cards.claim: JJ explained that Bitcoin's original script system calls FindAndDelete on the previous output script, removing the current signature from it.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: So there's a function that gets called on the previous output script called find and delete.

cards.claim: JJ explained that FindAndDelete only mattered in practice because of a SIGHASH_SINGLE bug in Satoshi's original implementation.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: So signatures in Bitcoin have different SIG hash types, and one of them is SIG hash single, but there was a bug in that implementation

cards.claim: JJ credited Peter Todd with discovering the SIGHASH_SINGLE abuse in Bitcoin's original script implementation.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: Peter Todd was actually the one who discovered this.

cards.claim: JJ said Peter Todd forked a couple of custom implementations by broadcasting a transaction that abused the SIGHASH_SINGLE behavior.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: He ended up forking a couple of custom implementations by putting a transaction out there that abused this

cards.claim: JJ warned that a custom script implementation that lacks these quirks could be confused by a crafted script and would fail to validate the chain.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: it's possible an attacker could confuse it by crafting some really weird script, which would be seen as valid by the Bitcoin network, but not by this custom script implementation.

cards.claim: JJ said bcoin was started by his friend Fedor in 2014 as a simple SPV wallet library.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: Bitcoin was started by my friend Fedor in 2014.

cards.claim: JJ predicted that after Bitfinex, many people would realize they need total autonomy over their wallet and system.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: after Bitfinex happened, I think maybe a lot of people will start to realize that it is important to have total autonomy over your wallet and your system.

cards.claim: JJ said he mined Litecoin and Dogecoin in the early days on an old Radeon GPU.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: Yeah, man. I mined Litecoin and Dogecoin back in the day.

cards.claim: In 2016 JJ said he was building Blight, a Lightning Network implementation on top of bcoin.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: lately I've actually been focusing on another project that sits on top of Bcoin which is which I'm calling B-Light or Blight

cards.claim: A host argued that if one implementation ends up ruling the network, it must be technically correct, since past library bugs should not repeat.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: if one implementation ends up ruling them all, you want that implementation to make sure it's technically correct.

cards.claim: JJ defined Bitcoin in ten words or fewer as a way to stop people from cheating without a central authority.
cards.speaker: JJ
cards.quote: Bitcoin creates a way to prevent people from cheating without some kind of sole supervisor.

title: TBP88 - Bitcoin Bike-Shed
